name: Europe
blurb: Old forests, rivers and shallow seas, under pressure from wildlife crime, forever chemicals, tree diseases, vanishing insects, trawled seabeds and fire in the south.

issues.title: The Glass Eel Trade

drivers.name: Dams and weirs that block migration

sites: An estuary where glass eels arrive
A weir that needs an eel pass

fact.text: Europol’s 2022 environmental crime threat assessment estimated that the illegal trafficking of European eels alone generates €2 to 3 billion in yearly criminal profits, and ICES notes that the European eel is classified as critically endangered by the IUCN.
fact.source: Europol, Environmental Crime in the Age of Climate Change: threat assessment 2022

issues.realWorld: Do not buy eel or unagi unless you know it is legal and sustainable, and support groups that remove dams and barriers from rivers.

issues.title: Forever Chemicals

drivers.name: PFAS from factories and fire-training sites
Persistent chemicals that do not break down

sites: A river downstream of a factory

fact.text: The Forever Pollution Project’s February 2023 map located nearly 23,000 sites in Europe contaminated by PFAS, plus 21,500 sites of presumptive contamination.
fact.source: The Forever Pollution Project (Le Monde and European media partners)

issues.realWorld: Choose PFAS-free products where labels say so, avoid non-stick and water-repellent products you do not need, and ask your local water supplier to publish PFAS test results.

issues.title: Ash Dieback

fact.text: A 2019 meta-analysis of ash dieback surveys in Plants, People, Planet found maximum recorded mortality of about 85% in plantations and about 70% in woodlands exposed to the disease for 4 to 20 years.
fact.source: Coker et al., Plants, People, Planet 1(1), 48–58 (2019), “Estimating mortality rates of European ash under the ash dieback epidemic”

also.source: ScienceDaily (5 December 2018), on the Wiley press release

issues.realWorld: Buy plants and trees only from nurseries that follow plant-health rules, never bring plants or soil back from trips abroad, and report diseased ash trees to your national forestry body.

issues.title: The Silent Meadows

drivers.name: Loss of hedgerows and wildflower meadows

fact.text: A 2017 study in PLOS ONE found a 76% seasonal decline in flying insect biomass over 27 years in 63 nature protection areas in Germany.

issues.realWorld: Let part of your garden grow wild, avoid garden pesticides, plant native flowers for pollinators, and ask local councils to mow verges less often.

issues.title: Trawled Protected Seas

fact.text: A 2024 report by the Marine Conservation Society, Seas At Risk and Oceana, using Global Fishing Watch data, found destructive bottom trawling still taking place in 90% of offshore EU marine protected areas, with 4.4 million hours of apparent bottom trawling in marine protected areas in the seven countries analysed between 2015 and 2023.
fact.source: Seas At Risk press release (16 April 2024), using Global Fishing Watch data

issues.realWorld: Choose seafood caught with low-impact gear and certified sustainable, ask retailers if it was trawled in protected areas, and back campaigns for enforcement in marine protected areas.

issues.title: Europe’s Burning South
sites: A village at the forest edge

fact.text: The European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) recorded 1,079,538 hectares burned in the EU in 2025, the highest total since its records began in 2006 and nearly double the 2006–2024 average.
fact.source: European Commission Joint Research Centre (31 March 2026), “2025 was EU’s most destructive wildfire season on record”

issues.realWorld: Follow fire-danger rules and bans in dry weather, never leave fires or barbecues unattended, and support grazing and forest-management schemes that reduce fuel.

issues.title: The Last Primeval Forest
sites: A primeval oak and hornbeam stand

fact.text: On 17 April 2018 the EU Court of Justice ruled that Poland’s forest management operations in the Białowieża Forest Natura 2000 site, which followed an authorised near-tripling of timber harvesting in one forest district, infringed EU law.
fact.source: Court of Justice of the European Union, Press release 48/18 (17 April 2018), Commission v Poland (Białowieża Forest), Case C-441/17

issues.realWorld: Buy wood and paper with FSC certification, support legal and campaigning groups that enforce nature law, and visit primeval forests on guided, low-impact trips.
